questions.text: What are tablespaces used for in PostgreSQL?

answers.text: To control the physical placement of database-object files
To separate transactions by isolation level

questions.explanation: A tablespace defines where data is stored in the filesystem and allows different objects to be placed on different storage devices.

questions.text: Which tasks can be solved with tablespaces? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Place frequently used data on faster storage
Place archival data on slower storage
Use free space on another filesystem partition
Automatically replicate an object to every server in the cluster

questions.explanation: Tablespaces allow physical storage to be selected for objects and therefore help manage available disk space and I/O characteristics.

questions.text: Which two tablespaces are created automatically when a PostgreSQL cluster is initialized?
questions.explanation: Cluster initialization creates the standard tablespaces pg_default and pg_global.

questions.text: Which statements about the relationship between databases and tablespaces are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: One tablespace can be used by multiple databases
One database can contain objects in multiple tablespaces
A database has a default tablespace
Every tablespace can belong to only one database

questions.explanation: Tablespaces are cluster-level objects. One tablespace can be used by different databases, and one database can place objects in multiple tablespaces.

questions.text: What is the pg_global tablespace used for?

answers.text: System catalog objects shared across the whole cluster
All temporary tables of every user

questions.explanation: pg_global contains system objects that belong to the whole cluster rather than to one database.

questions.text: Which statements about a database's default tablespace are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Database objects are created there when no other tablespace is specified
The system catalogs of that database are located there
template0 and template1 initially use pg_default
It must always remain pg_default and cannot be changed

questions.explanation: Every database has a default tablespace. Initially this is usually pg_default, but another tablespace can be assigned to the database.

questions.text: Which tablespace does a new database receive if CREATE DATABASE is executed without a TABLESPACE clause?

answers.text: The tablespace of the template database from which it is created
The tablespace of the first table created in it

questions.explanation: If TABLESPACE is omitted, the new database inherits the tablespace of the template database being copied. In a normal configuration this often results in pg_default.

source.locator: Section 23.6, inheritance from the template database

questions.text: Which requirements apply to the directory specified in CREATE TABLESPACE... LOCATION? Select all that apply.

answers.text: The directory must belong to the operating-system user running PostgreSQL
The directory must be inside PGDATA

questions.explanation: A user-defined tablespace is specifically a way to place data outside the main PGDATA directory. The directory must already exist, be empty, and be accessible to the PostgreSQL server.

source.locator: Section 23.6, CREATE TABLESPACE and LOCATION requirements

questions.text: Where does PostgreSQL place symbolic links to user-defined tablespace directories?
questions.explanation: For user-defined tablespaces, PostgreSQL creates symbolic links in PGDATA/pg_tblspc that point to the actual storage directories.

questions.text: Which mappings between standard tablespaces and directories are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: User-defined tablespaces are represented by links from PGDATA/pg_tblspc

questions.explanation: The standard tablespaces are stored directly inside PGDATA: pg_global in global and pg_default in base. User-defined tablespaces use links in pg_tblspc.

questions.text: How can the list of existing tablespaces be displayed in psql?
questions.explanation: The psql meta-command \db lists tablespaces. The same information is available from the pg_tablespace system catalog.

questions.text: Which PostgreSQL objects can be placed in selected tablespaces? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The documentation explicitly allows tablespaces to be selected for tables, indexes, and entire databases.

questions.text: Which parameter can be set so that CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX without an explicit TABLESPACE use a chosen tablespace?
questions.explanation: A nonempty default_tablespace value is used as the implicit TABLESPACE for table and index creation when no tablespace is specified directly.

questions.text: Which statements apply to temp_tablespaces? Select all that apply.

answers.text: It affects placement of temporary tables and indexes
It affects placement of temporary files for some operations such as sorts
It can contain a list of several tablespaces
It defines the location of postgresql.conf

questions.explanation: temp_tablespaces is intended for temporary objects and files. Multiple tablespaces can distribute the corresponding workload.

questions.text: Can a tablespace be dropped while database objects are still stored in it?

answers.text: No; before DROP TABLESPACE, the tablespace must be emptied of objects
Yes; objects are automatically moved to pg_default
Yes, but only if the tablespace is used by several databases

questions.explanation: DROP TABLESPACE applies to an empty tablespace. A tablespace cannot be dropped while objects still use it.

questions.text: What can ALTER TABLESPACE change? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Tablespace parameters through SET and RESET
The physical LOCATION path of an existing tablespace through a special LOCATION clause

questions.explanation: PostgreSQL 16 ALTER TABLESPACE syntax includes RENAME, OWNER, SET, and RESET. It does not provide LOCATION for changing the physical path.

questions.text: Which command sets random_page_cost = 1.1 for the pg_default tablespace?
questions.explanation: Per-tablespace parameters are configured with ALTER TABLESPACE ... SET (...). This is the method proposed in the additional practice.

questions.text: Which tablespace parameters are supported by ALTER TABLESPACE ... SET in PostgreSQL 16? Select all correct answers.
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL 16 documentation for ALTER TABLESPACE lists seq_page_cost, random_page_cost, effective_io_concurrency, and maintenance_io_concurrency.

questions.text: What does lowering random_page_cost relative to seq_page_cost imply for plan selection?

answers.text: The planner considers random access relatively less expensive, which can make index access more attractive
PostgreSQL automatically moves indexes to pg_global

questions.explanation: The additional practice notes that the smaller the cost ratio of random to sequential reads, the more often the planner may prefer index access over a sequential scan.

questions.text: Which actions create a user tablespace, make it the default for a new database, and verify its storage location? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Make it the default tablespace for template1 and create a new database
Find the symbolic link to the created tablespace directory inside PGDATA
Move the pg_global directory to another server without stopping PostgreSQL

questions.explanation: The exercise covers the full lifecycle of a user-defined tablespace: creation, template inheritance by a new database, the physical link in PGDATA, and later removal.
